sections.h2: Marion County and its tax classes
sections.html:
Fairmont is the seat of Marion County, a north-central West Virginia county along the Monongahela River. Fairmont, Mannington and Pleasant Valley are the cities, and the towns include Fairview, Barrackville, Farmington, Grant Town, Monongah, Rivesville, Whitehall and Worthington. Interstate 79 crosses the county.

Your tax category depends on whether the house sits in a town or in open country, since property inside a municipality is taxed in a different class from property outside it. The county has three magisterial districts: Middletown, Palatine and West Augusta. For the 2025 tax year the county purposes levy is $17,930,663, and $6,143,873 of that comes from excess levies that voters approved.

sections.h2: Older houses and what lenders want
sections.html:
Coal and the railroad built Marion County, and the age of its houses still shows it. The median Marion County home was built in 1960. Houses of that age often need roofs, wiring or foundation work before a mortgage lender will accept them, so sellers who cannot or do not want to spend that money often look at selling as-is.

The assessor's property record cards dating from 2001 can be searched online. Read yours before the February review so you can see how the assessor describes square footage and condition.

The Sheriff mails statements and starts collecting on July 15, with a 2.5 percent discount if the first half is paid by September 1. Interest of 9 percent a year, or 0.75 percent a month, applies to unpaid first-half tax from October 2.

DateWhat happens
July 1Assessment day for the following year's taxes
July 15Statements mailed and collection begins
September 1Last day for the 2.5 percent first-half discount
October 29 percent annual interest starts on first half
March 2Second-half discount ends
April 2Interest applies to second half; only full-year payment accepted
May 1Unpaid tax published as delinquent, fees added
October 31Delinquent real estate taxes certified to the State

After April 2 only a full-year payment is accepted. A seller who lets the spring installment slip can end up needing more cash at closing than expected.

The Sheriff acts as tax collector and treasurer from the first floor of the J. Harper Meredith Building, 200 Jackson Street, Room 101, Fairmont, WV 26554. Mail goes to PO Box 1348, Fairmont, WV 26555-1348. The phone is 304-367-5310, and the posted hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Online tax inquiry and payments are listed at wvpropertytaxes.com, with a Software Systems portal for the Marion County search.
  • Personal property assessment questions can go to the assessor at 367-5413.
  • Around September 1 the office notifies registered owners and lienholders by certified mail when property is headed toward the lien process.

sections.h2: Who sells delinquent tax liens now?
sections.html:
The West Virginia State Auditor does, since the Legislature passed Senate Bill 552. County sheriffs no longer conduct the sale of delinquent real estate tax liens. At the close of business on October 31 each year the Sheriff must certify the list of delinquent properties to the State Auditor's Office.

After that point an owner redeems through the Auditor's Office, not the sheriff. Chapter 11A of the West Virginia Code has the full text. If your Marion County house shows unpaid tax, move before October 31. After certification the cost and the paperwork both go up, and you deal with a state office in Charleston rather than the courthouse in Fairmont.

A cash sale can happen before or after certification, but earlier is simpler. We buy houses as-is in Fairmont, Mannington, Monongah and the rest of Marion County, and the payoff is handled at closing.

Protests go to the Marion County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which begins meeting February 1 and ends no later than the last day of February. West Virginia assesses at 60 percent of true and actual value, so the board checks that your number does not exceed that share of what the house is worth.

You can appeal the board's order to the Office of Tax Appeals by March 31, and the proof standard throughout is a preponderance of the evidence.

Bring the evidence with you. A written repair estimate, photos of a failing foundation or roof and two or three recent nearby sale prices carry more weight than a general complaint that the bill feels high.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller with open tax
sections.html:
Begin with a call to 304-367-5310 for the balance on each year. Ask whether the May 1 publication has already added fees, and whether any notice by certified mail has gone out. Next, ask the title company to order the payoff so it matches the date you plan to close, because interest at 0.75 percent a month keeps adding to the number. Finally, make sure the deed is ready and that the person signing has authority to do so, which matters most with an inherited house.

If the house is a rental, expect the Class IV bill to be the larger one and the payoff reflects that. Owners who bring the payoff, the latest statement and the deed to the title company usually close faster. Keep a copy of every receipt from the Sheriff's office, since the online search is the first place a buyer's agent will look for proof that a year is paid.

Owners 65 and older, or permanently and totally disabled, may claim the $20,000 homestead exemption after meeting the state residency rule. Ask the assessor how to file, and confirm it is on record before you list.

State law caps the regular levy for each kind of taxing body and each class of property, in cents per $100 of assessed value. The county sets the actual rate within those caps, and voters can add excess levies by referendum, which Marion County does use.

For Class II owner-occupied property the ceilings are 0.50 for the state, 28.60 for the county, 45.90 for schools and 25.00 for a municipality. Class III and Class IV double the state, county and school figures, and Class IV adds a municipal ceiling of 50.00. The state lists totals of $1.00, $1.50 and $2.00 per $100 for Classes II, III and IV, so a rental or vacant house can cost about twice as much to carry as the same house occupied by its owner.

If you own a Marion County rental and want out, call (424) 435-2326 for an as-is cash offer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Marion County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Sheriff's Tax Office, 200 Jackson Street, Room 101, Fairmont, WV 26554, or mail to PO Box 1348, Fairmont, WV 26555-1348. Online payment is available through the county's tax portal.

faqs.q: What is the Marion County first-half discount deadline?
faqs.a: Pay by September 1 to earn the 2.5 percent discount. Interest of 9 percent a year starts on October 2 for unpaid first-half tax.

faqs.q: Who runs the delinquent tax lien sale in Marion County?
faqs.a: The State Auditor's Office does. The Sheriff certifies the delinquent list to the Auditor by October 31 each year, and owners redeem through the Auditor.

faqs.q: What is Marion County's phone number for taxes?
faqs.a: The Sheriff's Tax Office is at 304-367-5310, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marion County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the payoff from your proceeds at closing, and an earlier sale avoids the extra fees that are added as the calendar moves forward.
